page: Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 1024.0 GB of RAM, offering 16.0 GB per core. The server includes 2199 GB of local SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate distinct characteristics influenced by the instance architecture. Single-core throughput ranks in the lower tier, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 915.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1038.39. In contrast, multi-threaded performance settles into the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9716.0 and a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 43761.68. Synthetic memory evaluations indicate solid throughput, reaching 215.58 GB/sec in large-block uncached read tests, while write bandwidth achieves 89.42 GB/sec.

Workload testing highlights capabilities suitable for memory-dense and multi-threaded enterprise processing. PassMark database operations scored 18057.18, and Redis throughput reached 40.5 million SET operations per second. However, compute tasks requiring single-threaded speed or specialized AI text generation exhibit weak results, with small-model LLM generation producing 36.53 tokens per second. Consequently, the M64s delivers balanced resource efficiency primarily for large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, and large-scale data processing workloads that require substantial RAM capacity rather than peak single-thread execution.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong uncached read memory bandwidth of 215.58 GB/sec, alongside average multi-core results such as a PassMark CPU score of 35325.17 and Redis performance of 40.5 million SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core processing metrics rank in the bottom tiers, reflecting lower per-core execution speeds. The server represents an efficient deployment platform for high-capacity in-memory databases, operational caching infrastructure, and enterprise data processing systems prioritizing large RAM density over per-thread compute speed.
